response.sql: WITH counts AS (SELECT f.film_id, COUNT(fa.actor_id) AS n FROM film f LEFT JOIN film_actor fa ON fa.film_id = f.film_id GROUP BY f.film_id), avg1 AS (SELECT AVG(n) AS a1 FROM counts), s1 AS (SELECT c.film_id, c.n, c.n - avg1.a1 AS ex1 FROM counts c CROSS JOIN avg1 WHERE c.n > avg1.a1), avg2 AS (SELECT AVG(n) AS a2 FROM s1), s2 AS (SELECT s1.film_id, s1.n, s1.ex1, s1.n - avg2.a2 AS ex2 FROM s1 CROSS JOIN avg2 WHERE s1.n > avg2.a2) SELECT SUM(n) AS total_actor_count, AVG(ex1) AS avg_excess_over_first_avg, AVG(ex2) AS avg_excess_over_second_avg FROM s2

assumptions.assumption: Actor count per film is the number of film_actor rows (COUNT of actor_id); films with none get 0 via LEFT JOIN.
If no films remain, the aggregates return NULL in a single row (SUM of nothing is NULL, not 0).
